Count the rows in each group (no additional grouping)

Source: R/count.R
tally.tbl_gpu.Rd

Like count.tbl_gpu(), but without any ...: aggregates exactly the groups x already has (or all rows, if ungrouped). Sugar over summarise.tbl_gpu().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
tally(x, wt = NULL, sort = FALSE, name = NULL)

Arguments

x

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

wt

Optional weight column/expression – as count.tbl_gpu().

sort

If TRUE, sorts the result in descending order of the count column.

name

The name of the count column. If NULL (default), uses "n", or "nn"/"nnn"/... if "n" already names one of x's group columns (note: unlike add_count.tbl_gpu()/dplyr::add_tally(), this check is against the GROUP columns only, not every column – verified empirically against dplyr 1.2.1, see this file's header comment).

Value

A tbl_gpu with the count column appended. If x was grouped by more than one column, the result's grouping drops only the LAST grouping column (matching summarise()'s default .groups = "drop_last" behavior for a real grouped_df – this is tally()'s own rule, and is NOT the same as count.tbl_gpu()'s "restore original grouping in full" rule; see this file's header comment).

See also

count.tbl_gpu

Examples

library(dplyr)
if (has_gpu()) {
  gpu_mtcars <- tbl_gpu(mtcars)
  gpu_mtcars |> group_by(cyl) |> tally() |> collect()
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>     cyl     n
#>   <dbl> <int>
#> 1     4    11
#> 2     6     7
#> 3     8    14
